U/S 3, 4 AND 6 REGISTERED BY THE FIRST RESPONDENT POLCIE I.E., ARAKALAGUD POLICE AGAINST THE PETITIONER WHICH IS NOW PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE, FTSC-1, AT HASSAN AND GRANT SUCH OTHER RELIEF/S.

ORDER This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge the petitioner on bail in Spl.C.No.232/2023 pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, at Hassan,
2. Heard both sides and perused the material on record.
3.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, FTSC-I, at Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Charge sheet is filed against the petitioner/accused in connection with Crime No.66/2023 registered at Arakalagud Police Station, Hassan, for the NC: 2024:KHC:1877 offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Section 3, 4 and 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

4. The petitioner is accused of committing Penetrative Sexual Assault on a minor girl aged about 6 years on 14.03.2023 at about 11:00 a.m.,
5.
The victim's statement has been recorded under Section 164(5) of Cr.P.C.

6. The learned Sessions Judge while dismissing the petition seeking bail, has observed that, during the investigation victim was produced before the Magistrate for statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as before the doctor for medical examination.
The doctor has examined the victim and collected certain biological samples and referred the same for FSL, based on the lab report, final opinion is offered.

The petition was dismissed placing reliance on the statement of the complainant and the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. holding that there are primary evidence as well as circumstantial evidence at this stage.

sentences.text: The accused is aged about 19 years and he is said to be a student studying in I year PUC.

Since the FSL report is not yet received and the victim's evidence is not yet recorded, the petitioner is permitted to move the Sessions Court by filing a bail application afresh after recording the evidence of the complainant and the victim.

In that event, the learned Sessions Judge shall consider and dispose of the said application as expeditiously as possible, keeping in view the relevant provisions of the POCSO Act, 2012.
8.
With the above observations, petition is dismissed.
